query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Doping a small amount (~5 at%) of Cu into a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy increases its glass-forming ability and raises the thermal stability of the amorphous state by enhancing chemical and topological frustration through stronger Cu–P interactions.
generation.material_initial_state: Amorphous melt-quenched ribbons or castings of a phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy (e.g., (FeCoNiCr)0.8P0.2) produced at cooling rates ~10^5 K/s.
generation.intervention: Substitute ~5 at% of the base HEA (e.g., 2.5 at% Fe + 2.5 at% Ni) with Cu, yielding (FeCoNiCr)0.75Cu0.05P0.20.
generation.conditions: Applies to P-containing HEAs with P content between 10 – 25 at% produced by rapid quenching (10^4–10^6 K/s). Not expected to hold if P < 10 at%, Cu > 10 at%, or cooling rates < 10^3 K/s.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced atomic size mismatch and negative mixing enthalpy between Cu and P leading to locally favored Cu–P clusters dispersed in the amorphous matrix.
generation.mechanism: Cu–P strong bonding and increased size mismatch raise chemical and topological frustration, slowing nucleation and growth of crystalline phases, thereby improving glass-forming ability and increasing crystallization onset temperature (T_x).
generation.predicted_outcome: Critical casting thickness for full glass formation doubles (e.g., from ~0.5 mm to ~1 mm) and ΔT_x (T_x−T_g) increases by ~15–25 K relative to the undoped baseline.
generation.baseline: Same P-containing HEA composition without Cu addition.
generation.boundary: Effect diminishes if P < 10 at% or when total cooling rate falls below ~10^3 K/s; may reverse if Cu > 10 at% due to Cu-rich crystalline phase formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two series of melt-quenched ribbons: (a) baseline (FeCoNiCr)0.8P0.2 and (b) Cu-doped (FeCoNiCr)0.75Cu0.05P0.20. Vary wheel speed to map critical thickness limits and perform DSC scans to determine T_g and T_x.
measurements: critical casting thickness for full amorphous structure (via XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Cu-doped alloy shows ≤5% change in critical thickness and ΔT_x relative to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
